first_impression.reaction: My assistant put this on the shortlist because we haven't settled on a month. The first line doesn't pretend there's one right answer, and I like that. It sounds like people who've been asked this question too many times to bluff. Her summary: June to August is dry and hot, Corfu stays wetter, the Cyclades are windy, and the church closes some dates. I read the intro, the month notes for June and September, and the close. The weather table and station notes are for her.

journey.quote: When to get married in Greece has no single answer, and any guide that names one month for every couple is guessing.
journey.reaction: Good. Calm and confident, nothing eager about it. This is the tone I'd expect from someone I'd let near my family.

journey.quote: The months that work for you depend on four things: the island, how well your guests cope with heat, whether you want a church ceremony, and how long everyone will stay.
journey.reaction: Sensible framing. With three hundred guests across three countries, 'how long everyone will stay' is the real question, so I'm glad it's there.

journey.section: How to read the weather figures
journey.quote: The Rodos and Heraklion figures cover 1955 to 2010, Chania Souda covers 1958 to 2010 and Kerkyra covers 1955 to 2010.
journey.reaction: Fine for my assistant. I don't need to know which years a weather station covers. I skipped this section.

journey.quote: For a July wedding, that shapes the day: an evening ceremony, shade for the aperitivo, water at every seat, and shorter excursions for older guests.
journey.reaction: Practical, and my grandmother would be in that 'older guests' group. It reads as a team that's thought about the day as it actually unfolds, not just how it photographs.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds, so reconfirm departures.
journey.reaction: We wouldn't be putting our guests on public ferries. Fine as general advice, but it reminds me this is written for a different kind of couple.

journey.quote: In practice, that means guests should know how to reach you if plans change on the day.
journey.reaction: With a few hundred guests, 'how to reach you' isn't a phone number. It's a communications plan and people on the ground. The thought is right, but I want to know who actually handles that.

journey.quote: At Angsana Corfu, the Oribu Garden runs from April to October, while the larger Vertigo Sky Bar does not open for weddings until mid-May.
journey.reaction: Useful as an example of how venues set their own seasons. But a hotel garden and a sky bar don't tell me whether a whole property can be ours in peak season, and that's what decides the month for us.

journey.quote: September keeps summer's warmth with the edge taken off.
journey.reaction: One line and I have the gist. September is probably where we land.

journey.quote: Those are the Archdiocese's dates in Australia. For a church wedding in Greece, ask your priest and the local Metropolis.
journey.reaction: Careful not to overstate. I respect a guide that says where its knowledge stops.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Single point of contact, working in my time zone: good. 'Quoting in AUD' is odd for a family in Dubai and London, and nothing here tells me they've ever done a wedding my size.

unanswered_questions: In June to September, can a property on the Cyclades or Crete realistically be taken over exclusively for three or four days, and how far ahead does that have to be held?
Which months make it easiest to secure enough rooms of the right standard nearby for 200 to 400 guests?
Have they planned a wedding of this size in Greece in high summer, and how do they keep a few hundred guests comfortable in the heat?
Can our own security work alongside the venue's, and does the season affect that?
Is there a private or referral route to someone senior rather than a web form?
Can they quote in a currency other than AUD?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as a single point of contact, anywhere in the world, and confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' is package language. It makes me think of a list of what comes in the box, when I want to hear what's possible. It's small, but it's the last line I read before deciding whether to enquire.

would_share_with: My assistant, for the month-by-month table and the closed church dates
My mother, for the July heat notes and the older-guests line

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, matching your shortlisted months to venue availability, travel and guest stays, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: It's measured and doesn't oversell, which I respect. But it speaks to an ordinary couple: no word about scale, exclusive use or discretion, and I don't fill in web forms. If my assistant went through a referral, perhaps.

top_3_changes: In 'Which months suit your wedding', add a scenario for very large or exclusive-use weddings. Frame it as questions to ask, such as how far ahead a whole property can be held in peak months and whether enough rooms are available nearby, rather than as promises.
In the closing CTA, change 'confirms the inclusions in writing' to wording that doesn't sound like a package, such as 'confirms the scope in writing'.

Next to the Angsana Corfu venue-window examples, add one line saying that for exclusive use the venue's season and its peak-season availability both need checking, so a reader planning at scale sees the guide covers her too.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, discretion and exclusive use)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why
Deferred business details and transfers not treated as must-fix; no single best month, no prices and no crowd claims accepted by design; no request about sourcing

assumptions: Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour, within a 5-minute budget.
Guest count of about 300, within the card's 200 to 400.
No ceremony type is assumed; the Orthodox sections are read as general cultural awareness.
